top news.title: Sources: parts of the Trump administration are reigniting efforts to implement de facto bans on foreign open-source models, as Chinese AI models gain momentum

tweets.author: @davidsacks
tweets.text: Kimi K3 just fixed 15 critical security bugs that Codex and Fable refused because of “cyber guardrails.” There's no reason to limit American models on tasks that Chinese models handle without issue. We're only making ourselves less competitive.

tweets.author: @sophiacai99
tweets.text: There was a brief discussion about this recently, but the Commerce Department is *NOT* moving forward on banning Chinese models at this time, per person familiar.

tweets.author: @alexstamos
tweets.text: How hard is this to type, David? “The Trump Administration was wrong to ban Fable and I was wrong to support the ban.” Try it, I bet you will still get ringside UFC tickets.

sub_items.title: Chinese open models like Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max shift the industry's focus back to marginal costs and cost of goods sold, as inference costs scale with revenue
Chinese open models are proper competition that should be welcomed, not something to ban or treat as a danger, and open-sourcing is an old business strategy

top news.title: Judge approves Anthropic's $1.5B settlement with authors, the first major US case of its kind to settle; some authors opted out and have other ongoing lawsuits
AMD plans to ship Helios, its first rack-scale AI system to rival Nvidia, later in 2026 to Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, and others; Helios costs an estimated $5M+

tweets.author: @lisasu
tweets.text: Excited to expand our partnership with @Azure to deploy @AMD Helios with our newest MI455X GPUs, Venice CPUs, and Pensando networking. Thanks @satyanadella @scottgu for the continued partnership. Proud of what our teams are building together!

tweets.author: @patrickmoorhead
tweets.text: ...There were no details provided on scale, deal size, deal length, or end customers.  There's the AMD-OpenAI deal, of course.  This is obviously a huge win for $AMD on the heels of announcing Helios with Meta and Oracle.  Note the 2H26 ship date.  If it were Q4 they would just say that right?  Could this mean August-September shipments begin?
